# S5 — Bound writable container layers and alarm on exited-container debris

## Why
Writable container layers can accumulate independently from BuildKit cache and image layers. Without a distinct cap/metric, exited-container debris can consume root while the operator only sees generic root pressure.

## What
Bound writable container layer growth. Prefer a Docker/runtime-supported storage quota when compatible with current overlay2/root filesystem; otherwise install a bounded periodic reaper for exited containers using Docker APIs such as `docker container prune --filter until=...`. Add observability for writable/exited-container footprint and a dedicated CloudWatch alarm at/near cap.

## Scope
In scope: runtime quota or stopped-container reaper, safety checks for live compose services and persistent volumes, metric emission, Terraform alarm, runbook updates, and tests. Out of scope: direct `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` deletion, BuildKit cache cap, journald, `/var/tmp`, and review scratch volume.

## Grounding
- Docker overlay2 docs describe writable container layers as the container `upperdir`/`diff` under `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` and warn Docker owns `/var/lib/docker`.
- Docker CLI docs support `docker container prune --filter until=...` for stopped containers.
- Compose services use persistent named/bind volumes for source-of-truth state, so stopped-container cleanup can be safe when scoped through Docker APIs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Writable container layer accumulation has an enforced bound or documented runtime quota; stopped-container cleanup is bounded and safe.
- [ ] Running containers, persistent named/bind volumes, and rollback images are not removed by the reaper.
- [ ] Observability emits writable/exited-container layer usage/cap metrics and Terraform declares a dedicated alarm wired to SNS.
- [ ] Runbook explains diagnosis/remediation and forbids manual overlay2 deletion.
- [ ] Targeted tests cover prune command construction/safety, metric emission, and alarm wiring.
- [ ] Portability criterion: solution uses Docker runtime APIs and local tests; no CI-provider-specific dependency is introduced.
